newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spring/White Wheat-Demand up for high protein.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spring/White Wheat-Demand up for high protein.

text.p: Basis bids for 14 percent protein spring and 13 percent hard red winter wheat rose on Wednesday as demand picked up, several cash dealers said.
"We're looking for higher protein," a Montana dealer said. "We've pushed our bids up a bit. It doesn't look like we're going to get very high proteins out of this year's crop."

Several dealers noted moisture stress late in the winter wheat growing season, which typically lowers protein levels. They said it was too early to determine the extent of the damage but said many buyers were covering needs now in anticipation of a shortage of 13 and 14 percent proteins.
Spring wheat crops in eastern Montana and North Dakota also struggled with dryness in May and June, dealers said.
The hike in basis levels coupled with gains in MGE futures brought cash prices up by nine to 19 cents a bushel. MGE July futures closed 8-1/2 cents higher at $3.71.
